reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource-level rubric, fresh-review framework, EvidenceVariable structure report, resource-review context, direct SearchParameters behavior finding, shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, the deterministic aggregate after forming the resource judgment, and sampled R4/R6 package StructureDefinitions/SearchParameters. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because the assigned resource is EvidenceVariable.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 EvidenceVariable was FMM 0/trial-use, so there is weak standards-stability pressure to preserve every R4 wire shape. That softens the burden for the core R6 redesign, but it does not eliminate the value of low-cost compatibility preservation for optional metadata, citation/discovery surfaces, or conformance metadata.

overall.oneLineConclusion: EvidenceVariable keeps its resource identity, but R6 replaces the required R4 characteristic/type-centered model with a substantially new variable model, making a resource-level migration program unavoidable while still leaving avoidable metadata and search-identity breaks worth preserving.

reasoning.thesisMd: The decisive fact is not the finding count; it is the shape of the model change. In R4, every valid EvidenceVariable required `characteristic` 1..*, with required `characteristic.definition[x]`. R6 has no `characteristic` and instead distributes variable meaning, modifiers, handling, categories, data storage, timing, constraints, missing-data meaning, and unacceptable-data handling across new top-level structures. A strict R4 instance therefore cannot simply be accepted as R6. The low R4 maturity makes the redesign plausibly acceptable, but it does not mean all compatibility losses are equally unavoidable.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: This is a major model remodel with stable resource identity, not a removed resource and not a mostly stable resource with isolated local breaks. The central required R4 backbone is gone, the optional primitive `type` code is replaced by R6 `handling` as CodeableConcept with different binding semantics, and several optional metadata/relationship fields are removed or reshaped. The resulting migration is semantic and policy-driven: converters need rules for R4 `definition[x]` choices, `exclude`, participant timing, `groupMeasure`, type/handling terminology, and `relatedArtifact` mappings.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the core characteristic remodel already forces a resource-level migration program, preventing every individual break has lower leverage than it would for a stable resource. But the right conclusion is not `migration-program-dominates`: some compatibility preservation remains cheap and useful. In particular, optional metadata fields and legacy SearchParameter canonical aliases can reduce catalog, conformance, and generated-client churn without preserving the whole obsolete R4 variable model.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Keeping R4 `characteristic` as a deprecated R6 backbone, or keeping `type` beside `handling`, would preserve more old instances but is not low cost because it creates duplicate core representations and conflict/precedence rules. By contrast, retaining deprecated optional `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic`, clarifying or transitionalizing `relatedArtifact` to `relatesTo`, and keeping per-resource SearchParameter canonical aliases appear more modest. Keeping `effectivePeriod` in the summary view would also have been cheap, but the impact is narrow and does not drive the resource-level posture.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior finding for EvidenceVariable is the canonical/metadata SearchParameter consolidation. Query codes often remain available through CanonicalResource or MetadataResource definitions, but canonical URL identity changes matter for CapabilityStatement metadata, registries, generated clients, and conformance tests. The shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search findings may affect servers that handle EvidenceVariable, but they are not EvidenceVariable-specific resource-level changes and were not scored as such.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate judged `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable` as `Partial` and `migrationShape` as `moderate-targeted-remodel`. I judge the migration stronger: removal of the required, central R4 `characteristic` backbone means every conformant R4 EvidenceVariable instance needs transformation before strict R6 validation, and the replacement is semantic rather than mechanical. I agree with the aggregate's compatibility leverage conclusion: preserve low-cost compatibility where feasible while expecting resource migration.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The element and behavior changes are directly observable with high confidence. Practical prevalence is less certain because R4 EvidenceVariable was FMM 0 and the supplied materials did not include an authoritative R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, official migration narrative, or broad production-use evidence.

findingConsiderations.title: Required R4 characteristic backbone was removed and replaced by a new variable model
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding drives the resource-level answer. R4 required `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` 1..* and required each `characteristic.definition[x]`; R6 has no such element and replaces it with a set of optional structures for definition, modifiers, data storage, timing, constraints, and missing/unacceptable data handling. That makes strict R4-to-R6 instance migration unavoidable. A deprecated legacy backbone would preserve wire compatibility but would duplicate the core model and is not a low-cost preservation strategy.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 type code was removed and replaced by R6 handling CodeableConcept
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This reinforces that the resource changed model, not just names. Populated R4 `type` is an unknown R6 element; generated APIs move from a primitive required-bound code to a CodeableConcept with example binding. Some mapping is straightforward (`continuous`, `dichotomous`), but other values and multi-coding/text cases require terminology policy. Once the larger remodel is accepted, this is mostly part of the migration program rather than the strongest avoidable break.

findingConsiderations.title: Several optional R4 metadata and relationship fields were removed or reshaped
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This remains standards-review-worthy despite the unavoidable core migration. The fields are optional, so they do not drive every-instance migration, but populated `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, or `relatedArtifact` become strict R6 validation breaks and can carry catalog, discovery, jurisdiction, topic, citation, or dependency meaning. Retaining at least `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic` as deprecated optional fields appears lower cost than preserving the entire R4 characteristic model; `relatedArtifact` needs explicit transition guidance to `relatesTo`.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding affects EvidenceVariable. The ordinary query code may survive through multi-base SearchParameters, but canonical SearchParameter URL identity is used by CapabilityStatement definitions, search registries, generated clients, and conformance tests. Because SearchParameter infrastructure has higher R4 maturity than EvidenceVariable itself and deprecated canonical aliases are a plausible low-cost transition, this remains a high-value compatibility-preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: status changed from mandatory in R4 to optional in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 instance break: every valid R4 instance already has `status`, and the same publication-status concepts remain available. It matters for R6-to-R4 conversion when R6 omits status, but R6 defines missing as unknown and R4 has an `unknown` code. It is a local down-conversion rule, not a reason to increase R4-to-R6 migration severity.

findingConsiderations.title: effectivePeriod was removed from the R6 summary view
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real API/projection concern for `_summary`, generated summary DTOs, sync views, or UI cards that expected applicability period in compact representations. It does not affect full-instance validation or the resource's semantic remodel. Keeping it in summary would have been cheap, but with FMM 0 and no specific deployment evidence it is best treated as a local migration note rather than a resource-level blocker.

findingConsiderations.title: Local warning constraints for name and URL changed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The changed constraints are warning-level quality checks. Warning-as-error QA pipelines and invariant-key dashboards may need updates, but ordinary structural validity is not broken. This is not a meaningful compatibility lever for the resource-level decision.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This represents the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. It may affect generic servers and clients that also handle EvidenceVariable, but it is not an EvidenceVariable-specific resource change and should not be used to inflate the EvidenceVariable migration conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm explicit R4-to-R6 EvidenceVariable migration guidance for `characteristic.definition[x]`, `exclude`, participant timing, `timeFromStart`, `groupMeasure`, `type` to `handling`, and cases that require extension preservation or manual review.

Revisit the optional metadata removals: retain deprecated `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic` if feasible, and document a precise `relatedArtifact` to `relatesTo` transition pattern for fields that cannot be represented directly.

For EvidenceVariable-capable systems, preserve or advertise legacy per-resource SearchParameter canonical aliases during transition, or define canonical-equivalence rules so conformance tooling does not interpret consolidated R6 definitions as missing support.
Treat `status` optionality, `effectivePeriod` summary removal, and warning constraint changes as implementation migration notes rather than primary standards-compatibility blockers.

caveats: No authoritative EvidenceVariable R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, StructureMap, or official migration narrative was supplied.
R4 EvidenceVariable was FMM 0/trial-use, so real-world R4 deployment prevalence is uncertain.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context because EvidenceVariable is not the Resource or DomainResource artifact.
